gen-gf-coming-soon-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Coming Soon sketches its letters like a quick pen note, with joins no thinner than the stems, over Noto Sans Elymaic. Down the page, the plain sans keeps everything open and easy.
gen-gf-coming-soon-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Twine-like and handmade, Coming Soon presses its looping strokes flat, then Noto Sans Ethiopic stands up sturdy beneath it. The heading does casual and personal best, while the body does tall, sturdy lowercase with hanging c terminals.
gen-gf-coming-soon-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Casual from the first word, Coming Soon writes with no swing between thick and thin. Noto Sans Georgian takes over with open curves and short ascenders, so its size can stay modest.
gen-gf-coming-soon-gf-noto-sans-glagolit: Noto Sans Glagolitic reads round and sturdy, its open shapes holding up well even at small sizes. Against the handwritten Coming Soon, whose curves never shift in weight, a long page would feel friendly.
gen-gf-coming-soon-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic has big, bead-like counters and round forms like open parentheses, all sitting in a plain sans frame. You could let it run fairly small beneath Coming Soon.
gen-gf-coming-soon-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Pen-and-paper casual up top, then tidy below. And Coming Soon's brushless, swell-free lines meet a plain sans in Noto Sans Grantha that never snags on a closed bowl.
gen-gf-coming-soon-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Noto Sans Gujarati is a plain sans whose curved strokes stop short before turning inward, leaving its counters generous. And a long page would move smoothly, with Coming Soon's unthinned curves adding a handwritten note on top.
gen-gf-coming-soon-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-: Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi reads chunky as a crayon mark, with terminals cut back to leave a big gap. Coming Soon, traced with one marker tip, can be larger while the sans stays small.
gen-gf-coming-soon-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Noto Sans Gurmukhi is a plain sans with terminals flaring outward like tongs. Coming Soon's spaghetti-like, same-width strokes give the pair its strongest quality: a loose handwritten voice sitting over a tidy, low-ascender body.
